name: GSP Crop Science Ltd
title: GSP Crop Science Ltd - 544733 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Agrochem maker passing through crude-linked cost hikes (10-15% price increase from 1 April) with patented mix rising to ~20% of revenue; no capacity additions or utilisation trend disclosed beyond formulations at 30-40% and technicals at 70-75%.

summary.headline: GSP Crop Science reported 9M FY26 revenue of INR1,114 crore and EBITDA of INR153 crore (up 32%), with PAT of INR75 crore versus INR59.6 crore.
summary.overview: Management described nine-month FY26 (to December 2025) as strong despite a prior-year monsoon disruption, with EBITDA up 32% YoY to INR153 crore and PAT rising to INR75 crore after a INR4.5 crore labour code exceptional provision. Management said the Middle East conflict raised crude-linked raw material, logistics and packing costs, and that price increases of 10-15% were effective from 1 April 2026, mainly in B2B where pass-through is faster. Patented products were about 20% of revenue in FY26, and management targets 40-50% of revenue from patented products over the next three years. The call was a Q&A-heavy session covering El Nino, input cost pass-through, plant utilisation and co-marketing partners.

segments.name: Domestic B2B
segments.commentary: About 40% of revenue; sells to agrochemical companies. Price increases pass through more readily here because pricing is elastic.

segments.name: Domestic B2C
segments.commentary: About 40% of revenue via about 5,000 distributors and 24 C&F locations. Price pass-through lags by two to three months; price increases began 1 April 2026.

segments.name: Export (B2B)
segments.commentary: About 20% of revenue across about 37 countries. Price increases passed to global B2B clients; a Brazil subsidiary has been opened for registering patented products.

segments.name: Patented products
segments.commentary: 102 patents granted and 108 in pipeline; 12 commercialised. About 20% of FY26 revenue; patented products carry a 20-25% gross margin premium over generics (55-60% vs 35-40% gross margin from material consumed).

guidance_outlook: Management targets 40-50% of revenue from patented products within about three years.
Growth target: a higher growth rate than the past three years by a further 5-7% over the next three years; no formal revenue or margin guidance given.
Price increases of 10-15% were implemented from 1 April 2026 to offset crude-linked cost increases.
Plan to launch one or two patented products per year.
Management said current plant capacity is sufficient to cover about three years of strategy, with peak revenue potential of about INR1,900-2,000 crore before de-bottlenecking.
capex_capacity: Technical plants: one near Ahmedabad and the largest at Nandesari, running at 70-75% utilisation; peak utilisation of about 90% is achievable.
Formulation plants at 30-40% utilisation, reflecting seasonality; they are simple mixing and grinding operations.
Intermediate manufacturing unit started last year to reduce dependence on China.
Capex plans and amounts were not discussed on the call.
demand_pricing: Management said El Nino forecast has limited impact because paddy (about 40% of consumption) is irrigated.
Fertiliser shortages and high prices are expected to push farmers toward nutrition and biostimulant products (seaweed, amino acids); the company sells three to four such products.
Crude-linked raw material costs rose; Chinese logistics costs have nearly doubled as ship availability fell.
Imported raw materials are held at about 45 days of inventory; no supply disruption yet, but management flagged risk if the conflict extends by another month.
PCT-410 (three-way seed treatment) scaled to INR50-70 crore in two to three years.
Sales team of about 300 with 30-35 marketing staff; co-marketing partners include Rallis, Sumitomo Chemical, Mankind Agri and Chambal Fertilizers (white-label model).

qa_highlights.question: How should FY27 be viewed given the El Nino forecast for Kharif?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said paddy, which is about 40% of consumption and largely irrigated, should limit El Nino exposure.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the Middle East conflict on sourcing, energy and pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Crude-linked raw materials and logistics rose (China logistics about double); price increases of 10-15% were taken from 1 April, with 45 days of imported raw material inventory held and no production disruption yet.

qa_highlights.question: Will gross profit per kg hold after the price increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Shail Shah said gross profit per kg should broadly hold because cost increases are passed through; B2C has a lag, and B2B is more elastic.

qa_highlights.question: How many patented products are commercialised and what share of revenue do they represent?
qa_highlights.answer: 12 of 102 patents are commercialised; about 20% of FY26 revenue came from patented products, with one new product launched in FY26 (an insecticide-fungicide mix for paddy).

qa_highlights.question: What are the plant utilisation levels and revenue potential at peak?
qa_highlights.answer: Technical plants run at 70-75% and formulations at 30-40%; peak utilisation near 90% could support about INR1,900-2,000 crore revenue, with de-bottlenecking possible.

qa_highlights.question: Are patented products being exported, and why are launches slow?
qa_highlights.answer: A Brazil subsidiary is registering patented products; registration takes about five years, so management targets one or two launches per year.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation from crude, China intermediates and petrochemical packaging; pass-through lags in B2C (two to three months).
Supply risk if the Middle East conflict and shipping disruption extend beyond about one more month.
Raw material availability for a few critical imported inputs.
Channel inventory and generic competition constraining B2C price increases.
Labour code impact (INR4.5 crore exceptional provision) and whether further provisions arise.
Ramp-up of the FY26 patented launch and the 40-50% patented revenue target.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and pricing power, especially on B2B pass-through. Less precise on B2C timing, the three-year targets and capex, which management declined to quantify. Some answers were rambling, and the revenue figure was stated inconsistently (INR1,114 crore and INR1,150 crore).

financial_highlights.metric: Patented product share of revenue (FY26 to date)
financial_highlights.change: Up from about 3% three years ago per management

financial_highlights.value: Domestic B2B about 40%, domestic B2C about 40%, export about 20%

growth.why: Management targets growth 5-7 points above the past three years' rate over three years, backed by 10-15% price increases from 1 April 2026, a patented-product mix shift to 40-50% of revenue, and 1-2 launches a year; no formal revenue guidance, and current capacity is said to cover about three years at ~INR1,900-2,000 crore peak revenue, with no new capex quantified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management said gross profit per kg should broadly hold as 10-15% price increases from 1 April 2026 pass through the crude-linked cost rise, with B2B pass-through faster and B2C lagging 2-3 months; patented products carry 55-60% gross margin vs 35-40% for generics, but no margin guidance was given.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Technical plants run at 70-75% utilisation with about 90% peak achievable, and management said current capacity covers about three years of strategy at peak revenue of INR1,900-2,000 crore before de-bottlenecking; no new plant was discussed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets growth 5-7 points above the past three years' rate over three years, backed by 10-15% price increases and a patented mix rising from about 20% toward 40-50% of revenue; 9M FY26 EBITDA rose 32% to INR153 crore, though the price increases are a major contributor to any value growth and volume is not split out.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Technical plants at 70-75% utilisation with 90% peak achievable and about 3 years of capacity at INR1,900-2,000 crore peak revenue; management declined to quantify capex, so a new announcement is not signalled for the near term.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: 9M FY26 EBITDA up 32% to INR153 crore and PAT up to INR75 crore from INR59.6 crore, with price increases of 10-15% effective 1 April 2026, but management gave no formal revenue or margin guidance to raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Imported raw materials held at about 45 days of inventory, with management flagging supply risk if the Middle East conflict extends by another month; China logistics costs have nearly doubled and B2C pass-through lags 2-3 months.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management plans one or two patented product launches per year, with 102 patents granted, 108 in pipeline and 12 commercialised; one insecticide-fungicide mix for paddy launched in FY26, and PCT-410 scaling to INR50-70 crore in two to three years.

rows.label: 10-15% price increases effective 1 April 2026
rows.why: Price increases of 10-15% were implemented to offset crude-linked cost increases, with B2B passing through faster and B2C lagging two to three months.

rows.label: Brazil subsidiary for patented product registration
rows.why: A Brazil subsidiary has been opened, but registration takes about five years, so meaningful export revenue from patented products is unlikely within the window.

rows.label: Nutrition and biostimulant demand shift
rows.why: Fertiliser shortages and high prices are expected to push farmers toward nutrition and biostimulant products; the company sells three to four such products, with no volume figure given.

tone.note: Management was confident on B2B pricing pass-through, patented-product mix and the 40-50% target, but cautious and vague on B2C timing, three-year targets and capex, which it declined to quantify; analysts probed El Nino, input cost pass-through, plant utilisation and patented launch pace.
